patient.name: Marcus Webb
patient.chiefComplaint: Stab wound to chest, worsening difficulty breathing

history.hpi: Patient sustained a single stab wound to the left lateral chest during an altercation approximately 10 minutes ago. Initially alert with mild dyspnea; over the past several minutes has become progressively more short of breath and anxious, now with visibly labored breathing.
history.lastOralIntake: Dinner approximately 3 hours prior to injury
history.events: Altercation with a single stab wound to the left chest from a folding knife; bystanders called 911 immediately

scene.dispatch: 29-year-old male, stabbing, conscious and breathing, residential street
scene.location: Sidewalk outside a residence, patient found leaning against a parked car
scene.safety: Police on scene, altercation participants separated, scene secured
scene.bystanders: Friend present, states patient was stabbed once during a fight and has been getting more short of breath
visualCues: Single 2 cm stab wound to left lateral chest at the 5th intercostal space
Patient sitting forward, visibly anxious and diaphoretic
No obvious external hemorrhage from the wound

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 29-year-old male with a single stab wound to the left lateral chest, now with worsening respiratory distress, absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Labored, asymmetric chest rise, diminished breath sounds on the left
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but weak and rapid, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Stab wound to left 5th intercostal space, no active external bleeding

expectedActions.shortAction: Needle decompression of left chest, 2nd ICS midclavicular line, for tension pneumothorax
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If absent or diminished breath sounds in a hypotensive trauma patient, especially those with chest trauma and/or tracheal deviation, consider tension pneumothorax and perform needle decompression of side without breath sounds or side opposite tracheal deviation
expectedActions.rationale: Relieves the obstructive shock physiology of tension pneumothorax.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply semi-occlusive dressing to the open chest wound
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For open chest wound, place semi-occlusive dressing
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents air entrainment through the wound while allowing trapped air to vent.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply supplemental O2, titrate to maintain SpO2 greater than 94%
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitor oxygen saturation (SpO2) and, if indicated, provide supplemental oxygen to maintain SPO2 greater than 94% and respiratory support if needed
expectedActions.rationale: Supports oxygenation while the underlying pneumothorax is addressed.

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes tension pneumothorax based on absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension, and performs needle decompression of the left chest.
Crew focuses on wound dressing and IV access without recognizing tension pneumothorax, delaying needle decompression despite absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension.

phases.name: Needle decompression performed
phases.description: Crew recognizes tension pneumothorax from the absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension in this penetrating chest trauma patient, and performs needle decompression of the left chest.
phases.triggerCondition: Based on decreased breath sounds on the left, tracheal deviation to the right, JVD, and hypotension in a penetrating chest trauma patient, the crew recognizes tension pneumothorax and performs needle decompression of the left chest at the 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Improved; rush of air heard on decompression, breath sounds now audible bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Semi-occlusive dressing applied to open chest wound

expectedActions.shortAction: Serially reassess breath sounds and hemodynamics en route for recurrent tension physiology
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Frequent reassessment of the patient is important. If patient develops difficulty with ventilation, reassess breath sounds for development of tension pneumothorax
expectedActions.rationale: Catches recurrence early, before the patient decompensates further.

expectedActions.shortAction: Repeat needle decompression of the left chest, same site, for recurrent tension pneumothorax
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: may need second or third needle decompression on same side if there is a rush of air but patient again has symptoms
expectedActions.rationale: Recurrence after an initial rush of air indicates the tension physiology has returned and requires re-decompression at the same site.

transitions.condition: En route reassessment reveals the patient's respiratory distress and hypotension have returned, indicating the needle has clotted or dislodged and tension physiology has recurred; the crew recognizes this and repeats decompression on the same side.

phases.name: Symptoms recur, repeat decompression
phases.description: During transport, the patient's breath sounds diminish again on the left with recurrent tracheal deviation and hypotension. The crew recognizes recurrent tension physiology and repeats needle decompression on the same side per protocol.
phases.triggerCondition: Several minutes after the initial decompression, the patient again develops absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation, and hypotension, consistent with the needle clotting off or dislodging; the protocol explicitly anticipates this and calls for a repeat decompression on the same side.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Labored again, diminished breath sounds on the left
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Pulses weak and rapid again, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Tracheal deviation to the right recurs

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue serial vital sign reassessment; minimize scene time and transport to trauma center
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Minimize scene time (goal is under 10 minutes) and initiate rapid transport to the highest level of care within the trauma system
expectedActions.rationale: Penetrating torso trauma with a treated tension pneumothorax still requires definitive surgical evaluation.

transitions.condition: Repeat decompression relieves the recurrent tension pneumothorax; breath sounds and hemodynamics improve and remain stable through transport.

phases.name: Repeat decompression successful
phases.description: Following the repeat decompression, the patient's breath sounds and hemodynamics improve and remain stable. The crew continues serial reassessment and completes rapid transport to the trauma center.
phases.triggerCondition: After the repeat needle decompression relieves the recurrent tension pneumothorax, the patient's breath sounds and vital signs improve; the crew continues ongoing reassessment and minimizes scene/transport time to the trauma center.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities

phases.name: Decompression delayed
phases.description: The crew focuses on the wound dressing and IV access without recognizing the tension pneumothorax. Without decompression, the patient's respiratory distress and hypotension progressively worsen toward obstructive shock.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew focuses on wound dressing and IV access without recognizing tension pneumothorax, delaying needle decompression despite absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation, JVD, and hypotension.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Severely labored, absent breath sounds on the left, shallow rapid respirations
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Pulses weak and thready, skin pale, mottled, and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Marked tracheal deviation to the right
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Minimal response, unable to speak in full words

expectedActions.shortAction: Immediately recognize tension pneumothorax and perform emergent needle decompression of the left chest
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If absent or diminished breath sounds in a hypotensive trauma patient, especially those with chest trauma and/or tracheal deviation, consider tension pneumothorax and perform needle decompression of side without breath sounds or side opposite tracheal deviation
expectedActions.rationale: Untreated tension pneumothorax progresses to obstructive shock and cardiac arrest; decompression can no longer be delayed.
